results.title: The μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{EF}\,p$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an atom $p$, $\mathsf{EF}\,p$ is the least fixed point formula $\mu X.\,(p \vee \Diamond X)$. It expresses that some state reachable from the current one satisfies $p$.

results.title: The μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{AG}\,p$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an atom $p$, $\mathsf{AG}\,p$ is the greatest fixed point formula $\nu X.\,(p \wedge \Box X)$. It expresses that every state reachable from the current one satisfies $p$.

results.title: $\mathsf{EF}$ is reachability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, every environment $\rho$ (an assignment of a predicate on worlds to each variable index), every atom $p$ and every world $w$, the μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{EF}\,p$ holds at $w$ in $\rho$ if and only if $p$ is true at some world reachable from $w$ in zero or more steps of the accessibility relation of $M$.

results.title: $\mathsf{AG}$ is universal reachability
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Kripke model $M$, every environment $\rho$ (an assignment of a predicate on worlds to each variable index), every atom $p$ and every world $w$, the μ-calculus formula $\mathsf{AG}\,p$ holds at $w$ in $\rho$ if and only if $p$ is true at every world reachable from $w$ in zero or more steps of the accessibility relation of $M$.

results.title: The formula $\mu X.\, \mu Y.\, X$ is false everywhere
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Kripke model $M$ and every environment $\rho$, the formula $\mu X.\, \mu Y.\, X$ holds at no world of $M$ under $\rho$. In de Bruijn form this formula is $\mu\, \mu\, x_1$: inside the inner binder, variable $1$ refers to the outer binder, not to the inner one.

results.title: μ-calculus formula closed at a given binding depth
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A formula is closed at depth `d` when every free de Bruijn variable is `< d`: only `μ` / `ν` increase the depth; `□` / `◇` do not bind variables and preserve it.

results.title: Closed modal μ-calculus formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A formula is closed when it is closed at depth `0`: every variable is bound.

results.title: Depth of a modal μ-calculus formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The depth of a formula: the length of its longest root-to-leaf path, counting each connective once.

results.title: Denotation of a closed μ-calculus formula is environment-independent
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A closed formula does not depend on the environment: environments agreeing below the depth give the same denotation.

results.title: Cantor-pairing number code of a μ-calculus formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An injective encoding of μ-calculus formulas over `ℕ` atoms as natural numbers, via the Cantor pairing function `Nat.pair`. This is a Nat code only, not a complexity input encoding: repeated pairing squares the code at every unary connective, so the binary length of the code of `box^d (atom 0)` doubles at each `box` and is exponential in `d`. Complexity statements use `muTokens` / `muDecodeList` instead.

results.title: Mukhamet'yanov–Fomin problem on centralizers of maximal order
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For an element $x$ of a group $G$ write $C_G(x)$ for its centralizer. This is the statement that for every finite group $G$ and every element $a \ne 1$ of $G$ with $|C_G(x)| \le |C_G(a)|$ for every $x \ne 1$ in $G$, every nilpotent subgroup $H$ of $G$ normalized by $C_G(a)$ (that is, $C_G(a)$ is contained in the normalizer of $H$) is contained in $C_G(a)$.

results.title: Centralizers of maximal order need not contain normalized nilpotent subgroups
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an element $x$ of a group $G$ write $C_G(x)$ for its centralizer. There exist a finite group $G$, an element $a \ne 1$ of $G$ with $|C_G(x)| \le |C_G(a)|$ for every $x \ne 1$ in $G$, and a nilpotent subgroup $H$ of $G$ normalized by $C_G(a)$ (that is, $C_G(a)$ is contained in the normalizer of $H$) such that $H$ is not contained in $C_G(a)$.

results.title: The constant coefficient lies in the ideal generated by the adjoined root
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, let $f \in A[X]$ be a polynomial, and let $\alpha$ be the image of $X$ in $A[X]/(f)$. Then the image in $A[X]/(f)$ of the constant coefficient $f(0)$ of $f$ lies in the principal ideal $(\alpha)$.

results.title: The constant term of an Eisenstein polynomial generates the maximal ideal of a DVR
results.caption: Lemma
results.summary: Let $A$ be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$, and let $f \in A[X]$ be a polynomial of positive degree that is Eisenstein with respect to $\mathfrak m$. Then $\mathfrak m$ is the principal ideal generated by the constant coefficient $f(0)$ of $f$.

results.title: Completeness passes to finite extensions of discrete valuation rings
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be discrete valuation rings, and let $B$ be an $A$-algebra that is finitely generated as an $A$-module and whose structure map $A \to B$ is injective. If $A$ is complete and Hausdorff for the adic topology of its maximal ideal, then $B$ is complete and Hausdorff for the adic topology of its maximal ideal.

results.title: Maximal ideals contract to the maximal ideal of a complete base

results.summary: Let $A$ and $B$ be commutative rings with $B$ an $A$-algebra that is integral over $A$, and let $\mathfrak p$ be a maximal ideal of $A$ such that $A$ is $\mathfrak p$-adically complete. Then every maximal ideal $Q$ of $B$ has preimage $\mathfrak p$ under the structure map $A \to B$.

results.title: Bitstring encodings
results.caption: Class
results.summary: A canonical bitstring encoding of a type $\alpha$ consists of an encoding map from $\alpha$ to finite lists of booleans and a partial decoding map from finite lists of booleans to $\alpha$, such that decoding the encoding of any $a \in \alpha$ succeeds and returns $a$.

results.title: Encoding function of a bitstring encoding
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a canonical bitstring encoding, the bitstring encoding of $a \in \alpha$ is the finite list of booleans that this encoding assigns to $a$.

results.title: Decoding function of a bitstring encoding
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a type $\alpha$ with a canonical bitstring encoding, bitstring decoding is the decoding function of that encoding: it sends each finite list of booleans either to an element of $\alpha$ or to failure.

results.title: Decoding inverts bitstring encoding
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a type with a canonical bitstring encoding. For every $a \in \alpha$, decoding the bitstring encoding of $a$ succeeds and returns $a$.

results.title: Self-delimiting form of a bitstring
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The self-delimiting form of a bitstring $(b_1, \dots, b_n)$ is $(\mathrm{true}, b_1, \dots, \mathrm{true}, b_n, \mathrm{false})$: each bit is preceded by $\mathrm{true}$ and the block is terminated by $\mathrm{false}$. In particular the empty bitstring becomes $(\mathrm{false})$.

results.title: Parsing one self-delimiting block
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Write booleans as bits, with true as $1$ and false as $0$. Reading a list of bits from the front, a $0$ ends the block, and a $1$ followed by a bit $b$ contributes $b$ to the payload. The result is the payload together with the rest of the list after the terminating $0$. Parsing fails if the list runs out before a terminating $0$ is read.

results.title: Bounded parsing of self-delimiting blocks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a bound $n$ and a list of booleans $s$, the parse returns the empty list of payloads if $s$ is empty. If $s$ is nonempty and $n = 0$ it fails. If $s$ is nonempty and $n = m + 1$, it parses one self-delimiting block from the front of $s$, then parses the remaining list with bound $m$, and returns the first payload followed by the payloads of the rest. It fails if either step fails. So the parse succeeds…

results.title: Parsing a list of booleans into self-delimiting blocks
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a list of booleans $s$, this repeatedly parses one self-delimiting block from the front of $s$ until $s$ is used up, allowing at most as many blocks as the length of $s$, and returns the list of payloads in order. It fails if some block fails to parse. The bound never binds, since every block uses at least one bit. So the parse succeeds exactly when $s$ is a concatenation of self-delimiting blocks.

results.title: Complexity classes

results.title: Polynomial-time computable functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be types with canonical bitstring encodings. A function $f : \alpha \to \beta$ is polynomial-time computable when it is polynomial-time computable with respect to the canonical bitstring encodings of $\alpha$ and $\beta$.

results.title: The complexity class P
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: P is the set of decision problems (functions from lists of booleans to booleans) that are computable in polynomial time by a deterministic multi-stack Turing machine, with respect to the canonical bitstring encodings of inputs and outputs.

results.title: The class coNP
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The class coNP. coNP is the set of decision problems $L$ whose complement, the decision problem that accepts exactly the bitstrings that $L$ rejects, belongs to NP.

results.title: Generator of the ancestral selection graph line-counting process
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The generator of the line-counting process of the ancestral selection graph with scaled selection coefficient `σ` (time in units of `2N` generations, the scaling of `generator`): from `n` lines, branching `n → n + 1` at rate `n σ` and coalescence `n → n - 1` at rate `C(n, 2)`.

results.title: Selection duality (Mano 2009)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Selection duality (Mano 2009) at generator level, with the line-counting process of the ancestral selection graph (Krone–Neuhauser 1997) as the dual: the Wright–Fisher generator with genic selection maps `y ↦ (1 - y) ^ n` to `C(n, 2) ((1 - x)^(n-1) - (1 - x)^n) + n σ ((1 - x)^(n+1) - (1 - x)^n)`. This identity holds for every real `σ`; the dual is a Markov chain only for `σ ≥ 0`.

results.title: Selection duality in operator form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The selection duality in operator form: `L_σ` applied to `y ↦ (1 - y) ^ n` equals the ancestral-selection-graph generator applied to `k ↦ (1 - x) ^ k` at `n`.

results.title: Stationary law of the ancestral selection graph line counts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The stationary law of the ancestral-selection-graph line-counting process with `σ > 0`: `π_k = (2σ)^k / k! / (e^{2σ} - 1)` for `k ≥ 1` and `π_0 = 0`, a Poisson`(2σ)` law conditioned to be positive. For `σ = 0` the stationary law is `δ₁`: branching vanishes, coalescence reaches state `1`, and state `1` is absorbing, so `π_1 = 1` and `π_k = 0` otherwise (the limit of the `σ > 0` formula as `σ → 0`).

results.title: Detailed balance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Detailed balance of the ancestral-selection-graph chain: `π_k · (k σ) = π_{k+1} · C(k + 1, 2)` for every `k` (the flux `k → k + 1` equals the flux `k + 1 → k`). This is an identity for every real `σ`.

results.title: Global balance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Global balance (stationarity `π Q = 0`) of the ancestral-selection-graph chain at state `k + 1`: the outflow `π_{k+1} ((k + 1) σ + C(k + 1, 2))` equals the inflow `π_k (k σ) + π_{k+2} C(k + 2, 2)` (for `k = 0` the inflow from the unreachable state `0` vanishes).

results.title: Stationary weights under selection are nonnegative
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `σ > 0` the stationary weights are nonnegative.

results.title: Generating function of the stationary law under selection
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The probability generating function of the stationary law: for `σ > 0` and every real `y`, `∑ₖ π_k y^k = (e^{2σy} - 1) / (e^{2σ} - 1)`.

results.title: Stationary weights under selection sum to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `σ > 0` the stationary weights sum to `1`.

results.title: Neutral stationary law is the point mass at one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The neutral stationary law is `δ₁`: its generating function is `y`.

results.title: Neutral stationary weights sum to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The neutral stationary weights sum to `1`.

results.title: Loss probability in Kimura's fixation formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The loss probability in Kimura's formula, written with positive exponents: for `σ ≠ 0`, `1 - kimuraFixation σ x = (e^{2σ(1 - x)} - 1) / (e^{2σ} - 1)`.

results.title: Loss probability from the stationary ancestral selection graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Loss probability from the stationary ancestral selection graph (Mano 2009): for `σ > 0`, `∑ₖ π_k (1 - x)^k = 1 - kimuraFixation σ x`, i.e. the loss probability of the favoured allele at frequency `x` is the probability that all lines of the stationary ancestral selection graph carry the unfavoured allele. Only the series identity is formalized; the sampling interpretation is not.

results.summary: If `u` is continuous on `[0, 1]`, differentiable on `(0, 1)` with derivative differentiable on `(0, 1)`, and `L u = 0` on `(0, 1)`, then `u = u(0) + (u(1) - u(0)) · S / S(1)` on `[0, 1]`.

results.title: Uniqueness of the scale-function ratio (Kimura 1962)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A function continuous on `[0, 1]`, differentiable on `(0, 1)` with derivative differentiable on `(0, 1)`, solving `L u = 0` on `(0, 1)` with `u(0) = 0` and `u(1) = 1` equals `S / S(1)` on `[0, 1]`.

results.title: Uniqueness for the Dirichlet problem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two functions continuous on `[0, 1]`, differentiable on `(0, 1)` with derivatives differentiable on `(0, 1)`, with `L u = L v` on `(0, 1)` and the same values at `0` and `1`, agree on `[0, 1]`. Together with `diffusionGenerator_integral_greenFunction` this identifies the Green integral as the solution of `L v = -g`, `v(0) = v(1) = 0` whenever it has this regularity.

results.title: Green's representation (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4; Karlin–Taylor 1981, Chapter 15)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let `g` be continuous on `(0, 1)` and assume the two halves of the Green integral are integrable away from the opposite boundary: `S g / (a ψ)` on `[0, q]` and `(S(1) - S) g / (a ψ)` on `[q, 1]` for every `q ∈ (0, 1)` (true for every `g` continuous on `[0, 1]` under genic selection, where `S / (a ψ)` is bounded near `0` and `(S(1) - S) / (a ψ)` near `1`). results.title: Dirichlet condition of the Green's function at zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Dirichlet condition at `0`: `∫₀¹ G(0, x) g(x) dx = 0` (for every `b`, `a`, `g`).

results.title: Dirichlet condition of the Green's function at one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Dirichlet condition at `1`: `∫₀¹ G(1, x) g(x) dx = 0` (for every `b`, `a`, `g`).

results.title: Wright–Fisher generator with genic selection as a general diffusion
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The general generator with drift `σ x (1 - x)` and variance `x (1 - x)` is the Wright–Fisher generator with genic selection.

results.title: Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection is regular
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection is regular.

results.title: Scale density of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The scale density of the Wright–Fisher diffusion with genic selection is `e^{-2σy}` on `[0, 1]`.

results.title: Kimura's formula as a corollary
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For genic selection the general scale-function ratio is `kimuraFixation σ p` on `[0, 1]`.

results.title: General Green's function agrees with the neutral Wright–Fisher one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The general Green's function of the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion (`b = 0`, `a = x (1 - x)`) is the neutral Green's function of `Sojourn.lean` for `x ∈ (0, 1)`.

results.title: Drift of an allele under selection with dominance
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The drift `2 c x (1 - x) (h + (1 - 2h) x)` of an allele at frequency `x` with genotype fitnesses `1`, `1 + h s`, `1 + s` (for zero, one and two copies), `c = N s`, time in units of `2N` generations (Kimura 1962). For `h = 1/2` it is genic selection with `σ = c`.

results.title: Diffusion with dominance is regular
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The diffusion with dominance is regular.

results.title: Kimura's scale-function ratio with dominance (Kimura 1962)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With `D = 2h - 1`, for `p ∈ [0, 1]`, `u(p) = ∫₀^p e^{-2cDx(1-x) - 2cx} dx / ∫₀¹ e^{-2cDx(1-x) - 2cx} dx`.

results.title: Sojourn density conditioned on fixation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The sojourn density conditioned on fixation, the Doob `h`-transform of the Green's function by the fixation probability `u`: `G(p, x) u(x) / u(p)` (Kimura–Ohta 1969; Ewens 2004, Chapter 4). At `p = 0` it is the junk value `0`.

results.title: Conditional mean time to fixation, backward equation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Under the hypotheses of `diffusionGenerator_integral_greenFunction` for `g = u` (the fixation probability), the function `w(q) = u(q) · ∫₀¹ G*(q, x) dx`, with `G*` the conditional sojourn density, solves `L w = -u` on `(0, 1)` (Ewens 2004, Chapter 4).

results.title: Neutral conditional mean time to fixation
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The neutral conditional mean time to fixation `t̄₁(p) = -2 (1 - p) log (1 - p) / p`, in units of `2N` generations (Kimura–Ohta 1969). It is meaningful for `p ∈ (0, 1)`; at `p = 0` the division gives the junk value `0` (the limit is `2`, see `tendsto_neutralFixationTime_zero`).

results.title: Neutral conditional mean time to loss
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The neutral conditional mean time to loss `t̄₀(p) = -2 p log p / (1 - p)`, in units of `2N` generations (Kimura–Ohta 1969). It is meaningful for `p ∈ (0, 1)`.

results.title: Neutral loss time equals fixation time at $1 - p$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Loss of an allele at frequency `p` is fixation of the other allele at `1 - p`.

results.title: The general `h`-transform specializes to Kimura–Ohta
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For the neutral Wright–Fisher diffusion (`b = 0`, `a = x (1 - x)`) and `p ∈ (0, 1)`, the total conditional sojourn time `∫₀¹ G(p, x) u(x) / u(p) dx` is `-2 (1 - p) log (1 - p) / p`.

results.title: Backward equation for the neutral conditional fixation time
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The neutral conditional fixation time satisfies the conditioned backward equation `L_0 (p · t̄₁(p)) = -p` on `(0, 1)`.

results.title: `t̄₁(0⁺) = 2`
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A new neutral mutation that is destined to fix takes on average `2` units (`4N` generations) to do so (Kimura–Ohta 1969).

results.title: Total expectation
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For `p ∈ (0, 1)`, `p · t̄₁(p) + (1 - p) · t̄₀(p) = -2 (p log p + (1 - p) log (1 - p))`, the unconditional mean absorption time.
